1.explanation:
1. src/js/components/Select/README.md – Shows how Select is used, its properties and theming hooks.  
2. src/js/components/Select/stories/components/icons – Contains the default down-arrow icon definition used by Select; critical for understanding its color and how it’s imported.  
3. src/js/components/Grommet/README.md – Describes the top-level Grommet component and the onDark mechanism, which should toggle icon/text colors when placed on dark backgrounds.  
4. src/js/themes – Holds the theme definitions (global.colors, control colors, onDark overrides) that govern default icon colors; you’ll need to inspect this to see why the arrow isn’t remapped.  
5. storybook – Contains the playground configuration and examples; helpful to reproduce the issue in an isolated environment and confirm what stories/styles are applied.  
6. src/js/utils – May include helper functions for color manipulation or onDark detection (e.g. utility for picking contrasting colors), which could be where the arrow color logic fails.
1.bug_scenario:
The user is placing the Grommet Select component on a dark (purple) background (“small” header area). In that context the default down-arrow icon renders in the same (dark) color as the background and disappears. In the second screenshot, on a white background, the arrow is visible (in purple). Key elements involved:
- Dark background container (purple header)
- Select input box (border, padding, text color)
- Down-arrow icon (SVG or Icon component)
- Grommet theming/onDark logic (should invert or remap icon color on dark surfaces)
